answer: A work-bonded identity registry makes each identity expensive to create and cheap to verify. An agent must lock a refundable stake and finish one public, checkable task before trading; its reputation stays tied to that single bonded record, like a bridge across a canyon that cannot be copied for free. A lone island of fake accounts earns no trust, since unbonded newcomers face strict transaction limits, and violet-flagged anomalies trigger a review that slashes the bond when one operator runs many shells. An attacker must pay the full cost for every fake, so mass forgery stops paying.
